steps.stem:
A youth movement chooses counselors for its summer camp. Every counselor who is chosen must meet at least one of the following two conditions:
A. He has at least two years of experience as a counselor.
B. He has completed a first-aid course and is older than 20.
In which of the following groups of candidates is there a candidate who cannot be chosen?
choices: Aya, 19, with three years of experience; Gadi, 23, with one year of experience, who has completed a first-aid course; Ronit, 20, with two full years of experience
Eli, 24, with four years of experience; Hodaya, 20, with one year of experience, who has completed a first-aid course; Yair, 19, with two years of experience
Dafna, 22, with two years of experience; Shaul, 25, with five years of experience; Mor, 19, with three years of experience
Adi, 26, who has no experience but has completed a first-aid course; Ben, 21, with two years of experience; Nili, 20, with three years of experience
explanation: Hodaya has only one year of experience, and although she has completed a first-aid course, she is not older than 20, so she meets neither condition. In (1) Gadi and in (4) Adi lack the experience but meet condition B, since each has completed the course and is older than 20; in (3) every candidate has at least two years of experience.

steps.stem:
Four candidates applied for a job as a guide at a city museum. These were the results:
- Eldad, who speaks English and French, was accepted for the job.
- Tzipi, who speaks English, was accepted for the job.
- Orna, who speaks Russian, was not accepted.
- Moti, who speaks Russian and Spanish, was accepted for the job.
Note: none of the four candidates speaks any language other than those listed above. Which of the following could not have been the requirement for being accepted for the job?
choices: Any candidate who speaks two languages is accepted, and any candidate who speaks English is accepted as well
All of the candidates are accepted, except those who speak one language only and that language is not English
A candidate is accepted only if he speaks more than one language or does not speak English at all
A candidate who does not speak English is not accepted, unless he speaks Spanish
explanation: Under (3) Tzipi, who speaks English and nothing else, could not be accepted, yet she was. Each of the other requirements fits all four results.

steps.stem: Amnon, Bracha and Gila live in a three-story building, one on each floor, not necessarily in that order. Each of them keeps one of these pets: a cat, a dog and a rabbit. Given: A. Bracha lives on a floor adjacent to the floor of the dog's owner. B. The owner of the rabbit lives on the second floor. Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: Gila is the owner of the cat
Amnon lives on the third floor of the building
Amnon is not the owner of the rabbit
Gila is not the owner of the dog
explanation: If Bracha lived on the first or third floor, the only floor adjacent to hers would be the second, whose tenant owns the rabbit, not the dog; so Bracha lives on the second floor and owns the rabbit. Amnon and Gila may be on either of the other floors, with either the cat or the dog.

steps.stem: Two novels and two cookbooks stand on a shelf in places 1 to 4, numbered from left to right. It is known that the two cookbooks do not stand next to each other. Which of the following additional facts would make it possible to determine with certainty the type of every book?
choices: Book 3 is a novel
Book 4 is a cookbook
Book 1 is a novel
No book stands next to a book of its own type
explanation: The cookbooks can stand in places 1 and 3, 1 and 4, or 2 and 4; a novel in place 1 leaves only 2 and 4. (1) and (2) each leave 1 and 4 or 2 and 4, and (4) leaves 1 and 3 or 2 and 4.

steps.stem: The statements made in the following conversation contradict one another. Tzila: "Yigal lends his books only to people who are older than he is." Eli: "I am younger than Yigal." Orna: "I am older than Eli and younger than Tzila." Yigal: "I have lent books to Tzila, to Orna and to Eli." Without which speaker's statement would the conversation still contain a contradiction?
choices: Tzila
Eli
Orna
Yigal
explanation: Tzila's and Yigal's statements together make Eli older than Yigal, while Eli says he is younger; Orna's statement plays no part in this. Removing Tzila, Eli or Yigal removes one part of the contradiction.

steps.stem: Einat, Hagai and Moti had to choose where their team would spend a day out: at the zoo, at the beach or at the science museum. Each of them expressed a wish. Einat: "I would like us to go to the beach." Hagai: "I do not mind where we go, as long as it is not the zoo." Moti: "I will be pleased if we go to the science museum, or if Hagai is pleased." The team went to one of the three places, and exactly one of the three did not get his wish. Which of the following is possible?
choices: The team went to the beach
Moti did not get his wish
The team went to the science museum
Hagai was the only one who did not get his wish
explanation: At the museum Einat is disappointed while Hagai and Moti are pleased, so exactly one wish fails. At the beach everyone is pleased. Hagai's wish fails only at the zoo, and there Einat's and Moti's wishes fail too; Moti's wish fails only when Hagai's does, which again happens only at the zoo.

steps.stem: Five contestants take part in a television quiz: Sarit, Amnon, Yigal, Tzipi and Eldad. In each round two contestants compete. The loser leaves the quiz, and the winner competes in the next round against a contestant who has not yet competed, until the fourth and last round. The following rule is known: if Sarit competes against a contestant who, in the previous round, competed against Amnon, Sarit loses; in every other case Sarit wins. If Sarit competed in the first round of the quiz, then -
choices: she lost in the second round
she won the last round
she lost in the first round
she lost in the last round
explanation: Every opponent Sarit meets after the first round is a newcomer who did not compete in the previous round, and in the first round there was no previous round; so the rule never makes her lose, and she wins every round including the last.

steps.title: Rules and arrangements — the method
steps.intro: Two question types — rules and arrangements — and combined ones.

tables.title: Rules questions
head: Way
How
rows: Take one answer, test it against every rule
Take one rule, run it through all the answers, cross out

tables.title: Arrangement questions
head: Step
What to do
rows: Circle the items you need to place
Sketch the slots — never solve in your head
Find an anchor: a clue that fixes an exact position
Chain the other clues onto it; loose pairs go at the side
Two items can swap → draw a two-way arc

tips: Each answer adds a new given? Test it alone — start again from the base givens.
Contradiction question: leave one statement out and test whether the rest still clash.
"Exactly N are true": place each answer as the situation and count what holds.

steps.stem: The house committee of an apartment building meets on the first Sunday of each month. A tenant who wants the committee to discuss a matter hands a note to the committee's secretary. If the note is handed in by the 20th of the month, the matter is discussed at the next meeting; if it is handed in later, the matter is discussed at the meeting after that. The chairman may postpone a discussion by one meeting, but no more. In which of the following cases was the procedure definitely not followed?
choices: Ronen handed in a note on March 25th, and his matter was not discussed until the May meeting
Sigal handed in a note in March, and her matter was not discussed until the June meeting, after the chairman had postponed it
The chairman postponed Doron's matter, and it was discussed at the May meeting
Orna handed in a note on March 10th, and her matter was discussed at the June meeting, after the chairman had postponed it
explanation: A note handed in on March 10th is due at the April meeting, and one postponement brings it to May at the latest, never June. In (1) a note handed in after the 20th is due in May, in (2) a note handed in after the 20th and postponed once is discussed in June, and in (3) nothing is known that rules out May.

steps.stem:
Avner, Eitan, Rivka and Tamar are sitting at a square table, one on each side, so that each of them sits opposite one of the others.
Given:
A. Tamar sits opposite the only man with glasses.
B. Avner sits opposite the only woman with a hat.
Therefore, it is not possible that -
choices: Tamar does not wear a hat, and Rivka sits beside Eitan
Eitan does not wear glasses, and Avner sits beside Rivka
Avner wears glasses, and Tamar does not wear a hat
Eitan wears glasses, and Avner sits beside Tamar
explanation: If Avner is the man with glasses, Tamar sits opposite him; but the person opposite Avner is the woman with the hat, so Tamar must wear the hat. Each of the other combinations fits some seating.

steps.stem: Five families live in five adjacent houses, numbered 1 to 5, on one side of a street: the Peretz, Sasson, Hadad, Ben-Ami and Gabai families. The Peretz family lives in house 1 and the Sasson family in house 2. Which of the following pieces of information, if added, would make it possible to determine with certainty where each family lives?
choices: The Hadad family lives next door to the Sasson family, and the Gabai family lives at the end of the street
The Ben-Ami family lives between the Hadad family and the Gabai family
The Gabai family does not live at the end of the street, and the Hadad family does not live next door to the Sasson family
The Hadad family and the Ben-Ami family live next door to each other
explanation: With houses 1 and 2 taken, (1) puts the Hadads in house 3 and the Gabais in house 5, which leaves house 4 for the Ben-Amis. Each of the other pieces of information leaves more than one possibility.

steps.stem: A community center charges 80 shekels a month for its pottery class; soldiers and pensioners pay half. For which of the following participants is there not enough information to determine how much they must pay this month?
choices: Tzipi, a pensioner who has attended the class for many years
Amnon, who is not a soldier
Pnina, who is neither a soldier nor a pensioner
Itzik, a nineteen-year-old soldier
explanation: Amnon is not a soldier, but it is not stated whether he is a pensioner, so he may pay either amount. Tzipi and Itzik pay half, and Pnina pays the full amount.

steps.stem: Four cars are parked in a row: two red cars and two white cars. The two white cars are not parked next to each other. Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: There is a red car at each end of the row
The two red cars are parked next to each other
At least one of the two cars at the ends of the row is white
At least one white car is parked between the two red cars
explanation: The white cars can stand only in places 1 and 3, 1 and 4, or 2 and 4, and in each case one of them is at an end. (1) and (4) fail when the white cars are in places 1 and 4, and (2) fails in the other two cases.

steps.stem: Ofra, Hanan and Varda are three siblings, no two of whom are the same age. Their mother mentioned that Ofra is older than Hanan, and their father added that Varda is not the youngest of them. Based on what the parents said, which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: Varda is the oldest of the three
Ofra is the oldest of the three
Varda is older than Ofra
Hanan is the youngest of the three
explanation: Ofra is older than Hanan, so she is not the youngest, and neither is Varda; the youngest must be Hanan. Who is the oldest is not determined, so (1), (2) and (3) are possible but not necessary.

steps.stem:
Three suitcases - a red one, a black one and a brown one - have different weights.
Given:
- The red suitcase is not the heaviest of the three.
- The brown suitcase is not the lightest of the three.
Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
choices: If the black suitcase is the lightest, then the brown suitcase is the heaviest
If the red suitcase is the lightest, then the brown suitcase is the heaviest
The black suitcase is the heaviest
The red suitcase is the lightest
explanation: If the black suitcase is the lightest, the red and brown ones remain for the top, and the red one cannot be the heaviest. (2) fails when the black suitcase is the heaviest, and (3) and (4) each fail in some order.

steps.stem:
Given:
A. Gali's salary is not higher than Ofer's salary.
B. Gali's salary is not lower than Nurit's salary.
Which of the following is not possible?
choices: Gali, Ofer and Nurit all earn the same salary
Ofer's salary is lower than Nurit's salary
Ofer's salary is higher than Nurit's salary
The three salaries are all different
explanation: Nurit earns no more than Gali, and Gali no more than Ofer, so Ofer can never earn less than Nurit. Equal salaries all round and three different salaries are both allowed.

steps.stem: The membership cards of a chess club are kept in a box, arranged from front to back by the month in which each member joined the club, from January to December. Cards of members who joined in the same month are arranged by the age at which they joined, with the card of the member who joined younger in front. There are four cards in the box: Zalman's, who joined in March at the age of 70; Ofir's, who joined in November at the age of 12; Tamir's, who joined in March at the age of 81; and Chen's, who joined in November at the age of 15. Which card is at the back of the box?
choices: Zalman's card
Ofir's card
Tamir's card
Chen's card
explanation: The month decides first, so the two November cards are behind the two March cards; of these, Chen joined at an older age than Ofir, so his card is behind Ofir's. Tamir was the oldest when he joined, but age matters only within the same month.

steps.stem: Every month Eli changes the code of his storeroom lock according to these rules: first he reverses the order of the digits of the old code; then he replaces every 1 with a 7 and every 7 with a 1; finally, if the old code ended in an even digit, he adds a 9 at the beginning of the new code. This month's code is 1784. What will next month's code be?
explanation: Reversing 1784 gives 4871, exchanging 1 and 7 gives 4817, and since 1784 ends in an even digit, a 9 is added at the beginning: 94817. (1) applies only the first rule, (2) forgets the last rule, and (4) adds the 9 at the end.

steps.stem: Adva, Benny and Gilit work in the same office. Two of them speak French, and two of them speak Russian. Adva does not speak French, and Benny speaks only one of the two languages. Therefore, Gilit speaks -
choices: both French and Russian
French only
Russian only
neither French nor Russian
explanation: Adva does not speak French, so the two French speakers are Benny and Gilit. Benny speaks only one language, so he does not speak Russian, and the two Russian speakers are Adva and Gilit.

steps.stem:
A catering company follows these rules when planning a menu:
- If a menu includes soup, it must also include bread, and it may not include salad.
- If a menu includes fish, it must also include rice, and it may not include soup.
- If a menu includes cake, it must also include salad, and it may not include fish.
Which of the following menus does not follow the rules?
choices: A menu that includes rice, salad and cake
A menu that includes soup, salad and cake
A menu that includes bread, rice and fish
A menu that includes soup, bread and rice
explanation: A menu that includes soup may not include salad (and needs bread). Each of the other menus meets every rule that applies to it.

steps.stem: Three members of a tenants' committee - Moran, Shai and Liora - have so far attended committee meetings as follows: whenever Shai came to a meeting, Moran came too, and Moran and Liora have never come to the same meeting. If the same is true of the next meeting, which of the following is not possible?
choices: Only Liora will come to the meeting
Moran will come to the meeting, but Shai and Liora will not
Shai will not come to the meeting, but Liora will
Shai and Liora will both come to the meeting
explanation: If Shai comes, Moran comes too, and then Liora cannot come. Each of the other situations breaks neither pattern.

steps.stem: A municipal swimming pool gives a discount on the annual subscription to residents of the city who are over 60, and also to anyone who swam in the pool at least 50 times in the previous year. Which of the following is definitely not entitled to the discount?
choices: A 70-year-old man who swam in the pool 20 times last year and 45 times the year before
A 45-year-old woman who lives in the city
A woman who moved to another city two years ago and swam in the pool 30 times last year
A 62-year-old resident of the city who swam in the pool 60 times last year
explanation: The woman who moved away is not a resident, so the first condition does not hold, and 30 swims are too few for the second. The 70-year-old man may live in the city, the 45-year-old woman may have swum 50 times, and the 62-year-old resident qualifies twice over.

steps.stem: Every morning a minibus stops at four stops, one after another - the school, the clinic, the post office and the market, not necessarily in this order. Yesterday one passenger got on at the school and got off at the next stop, the clinic, and another passenger got on at the post office and got off at the next stop, the market. Which of the following could not have happened on the same trip?
choices: A passenger got on at the clinic and got off at the next stop, the market
A passenger got on at the clinic and got off two stops later, at the market
A passenger got on at the market and got off at the next stop, the school
A passenger got on at the school and got off two stops later, at the post office
explanation: The clinic comes right after the school and the market right after the post office, so the order is either school, clinic, post office, market or post office, market, school, clinic. In neither order does the market come right after the clinic. (2) and (4) fit the first order and (3) the second.

steps.stem: On days when Shmulik does not work in the afternoon, he picks up his daughter from kindergarten; on days when he does, his wife picks her up. When Shmulik picks her up, he walks, unless it is raining, in which case he drives. Which of the following is possible?
choices: On Sunday it did not rain, and Shmulik drove to pick up his daughter
On Wednesday it rained, and Shmulik did not drive to the kindergarten
On Monday Shmulik worked in the afternoon, and he picked up his daughter from kindergarten
On Tuesday Shmulik did not work in the afternoon, it did not rain, and his wife picked up their daughter
explanation: If Shmulik worked that afternoon, his wife picked up the girl, so on a rainy day he need not have driven. In (1) there was no rain, so he would have walked; in (3) and (4) the wrong parent picked her up.

steps.stem: In a community garden, the following rule applies: whoever is the last to leave the tool shed must lock it, and whoever closes the garden gate in the evening must make sure that the shed is locked. One evening Menachem closed the garden gate. He noticed that the shed, which only Tova had used that day, was not locked, and he went home without locking it. Which of the following is true?
choices: Only Menachem broke the rule
Tova did not break the rule, since Menachem was the last to leave the garden
Both Tova and Menachem broke the rule
Neither of them broke the rule, since the rule does not say what to do when the shed is found open
explanation: Tova was the last to leave the shed and did not lock it; Menachem closed the gate without making sure that the shed was locked. Leaving the garden is not the same as leaving the shed, and making sure the shed is locked means locking it if it is open.

steps.stem:
Two rules are posted at a library:
1. Only readers over the age of 18 may borrow more than three books at a time.
2. Only people who have been members of the library for at least a year may borrow books for more than two weeks.
The librarian said that in order to answer one of the following questions she has to use both rules. Which question is it?
choices: May a 30-year-old reader who has been a member for three years borrow five books for a month?
May a 25-year-old reader who joined the library last month borrow two books for three weeks?
May a 15-year-old reader borrow six books for a week?
May a 17-year-old reader who has been a member for four years borrow five books for three weeks?
explanation: The 30-year-old's request is allowed only if he meets both rules, so both must be checked. The 25-year-old fails rule 2, and the 15-year-old and the 17-year-old fail rule 1, so in each of these cases one rule is enough to refuse.

steps.stem:
A kitchen cupboard has three shelves, one above another. One shelf holds plates, one holds cups and one holds pots, and no two shelves carry the same weight. It is known that:
- The heaviest shelf is next to the shelf with the cups.
- The shelf with the plates is neither the heaviest nor the lightest.
Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: The pots are on the top shelf
The shelf with the cups is not the lightest
The plates are not on the middle shelf
The plates and the pots are not on adjacent shelves
explanation: The shelf with the plates is of middle weight, so the heaviest is the pots or the cups; it is next to the cups, so it is the pots, and the cups are the lightest. The pots and the cups are on adjacent shelves, so the plates cannot be between them and are on the top or the bottom shelf. (1) and (4) are possible but not necessary, and (2) is false.

steps.stem:
The municipality gave the guard of a public park three instructions, and told him that if two of them conflict, the one listed first takes precedence:
1. He must not let dogs into the playground.
2. He must lock the park gate at eight in the evening, but must not lock any visitor inside the park.
3. He must water the lawns every evening.
In which of the following situations will the guard not be able to know how to act?
choices: At eight the lawns have not yet been watered, and watering them takes an hour
At eight there is still a visitor in the park, and he refuses to leave
A visitor asks the guard to let his dog into the playground for a few minutes
At eight there is a dog in the playground, and getting it out will delay the locking of the gate
explanation: Locking the gate and not locking a visitor inside are both parts of the same instruction, so the order of precedence does not help. In (1) instruction 2 comes before instruction 3, in (4) instruction 1 comes before instruction 2, and in (3) instruction 1 decides.

steps.stem:
Yesterday Tehila ran four errands, one after another: she went to the bank, the post office, the pharmacy and the supermarket, not necessarily in this order. It is known that:
- She went to the supermarket last.
- She went to the post office immediately after going to the bank.
- She did not go to the pharmacy immediately after the post office.
Where did Tehila go first?
choices: To the bank
To the post office
To the pharmacy
To the supermarket
explanation: The supermarket is last, so the bank, the post office and the pharmacy fill the first three places, with the post office right after the bank. Bank, post office, pharmacy puts the pharmacy right after the post office, so the order is pharmacy, bank, post office, supermarket.

steps.stem:
At a youth club, the following rules apply:
- Only club members may use the ping-pong table.
- Anyone may use the club's computer, but while someone is working on it, no one else may use it until they have finished.
- Only members may play the club's piano, unless the counselor has given someone else permission to play it.
Which of the following situations is possible?
choices: The counselor gave Kobi, who is not a member, permission to play ping-pong, and he played
Kobi, who is not a member, played the piano after the club's secretary had given him permission
Nachum began working on the computer, and while he was working, Kobi joined him at Nachum's request
Kobi, who is not a member, played the piano after the counselor had given him permission
explanation: The counselor's permission opens the piano to a non-member. (1) breaks the ping-pong rule, which has no exception, (2) lacks the counselor's permission, and (3) breaks the computer rule.

steps.stem:
Shiri, Nimrod and Hadar live in a three-story building, each on a different floor. It is known that:
- Shiri does not live on the first floor.
- The tenant on the second floor has a dog.
- Nimrod does not have a dog, and he lives on a higher floor than Hadar.
Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: Hadar has a dog
Shiri has a dog
Nimrod lives on the second floor
Hadar does not have a dog
explanation: Nimrod has no dog, so he is not on the second floor, and since he lives above Hadar he is on the third. Shiri is not on the first floor, so she is on the second and has the dog, and Hadar is on the first. Whether Hadar has a dog is not known.

steps.stem: Batya is preparing sandwiches for a family trip. In each sandwich there are two different fillings from among egg, tuna, cheese and avocado. Yoel will eat a sandwich only if there is egg in it, and he never eats avocado. Zohar eats only sandwiches with tuna, and cannot stand egg. Chanan wants cheese in his sandwich and refuses to eat tuna, and Tzvi eats only sandwiches with avocado, provided that there is no cheese in them. Batya wants to prepare one kind of sandwich that two of the children will eat. Who could the two be?
choices: Zohar and Yoel
Chanan and Tzvi
Tzvi and Yoel
Yoel and Chanan
explanation: A sandwich of egg and cheese suits Yoel, who gets egg and no avocado, and Chanan, who gets cheese and no tuna. Every other pair needs a filling that one of the two refuses.

steps.stem: Nissan buys a new pair of work shoes every year. In the store they always offer him two pairs, and he chooses one of them. Nissan prefers leather shoes to canvas shoes, and when both pairs are made of the same material, he takes the lighter pair; but if one of the pairs is waterproof, he takes it in any case. This year Nissan chose leather shoes that weigh 900 grams and are not waterproof. Which of the following could have been the other pair that was offered to him?
choices: Leather shoes that weigh 1.1 kilograms and are not waterproof
Leather shoes with rubber soles that weigh 800 grams
Waterproof canvas shoes that weigh 1.2 kilograms
Leather shoes that weigh 850 grams and are not waterproof
explanation: Of two leather pairs Nissan takes the lighter, so a 1.1-kilogram pair loses to the one he chose. (2) and (4) are lighter leather pairs and would have won ((2) would also win if it were waterproof), and (3) is waterproof.

steps.stem: Tzipora had two baskets of fruit. In the first there were two apples and a pear; in the second, an apple, a plum and a pear. She moved one fruit from the first basket to the second and one fruit from the second to the first. After this, each basket held two fruits of the same kind and one fruit of a different kind. Which of the following could not have happened?
choices: An apple was moved from the second basket to the first
An apple was moved from the first basket to the second
The pear from the first basket was moved to the second
The plum was moved to the first basket
explanation: If an apple came into the first basket, either a pear left it and it held three apples, or an apple left it and the second basket kept three different fruits. Each of the other moves is part of an exchange that meets the condition.

steps.stem: Grandmother Zelda served her three grandchildren a plate of cheese burekas, potato burekas and poppy seed pastries. Ohad eats only cheese burekas and potato burekas, Batel eats only potato burekas and poppy seed pastries, and Gal eats only poppy seed pastries. Each of the grandchildren ate at least one pastry. Which of the following is not possible?
choices: None of the grandchildren ate cheese burekas
All three grandchildren ate from the same kind of pastry
Two of the grandchildren ate from a kind of pastry that the third did not eat
Only one of the grandchildren ate potato burekas
explanation: Cheese burekas are eaten only by Ohad, potato burekas not by Gal, and poppy seed pastries not by Ohad, so no kind was eaten by all three. Each of the other situations can happen.
